prompt:
Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with wrist fracture after a side impact at intersection. The patient had 40 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1189; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment grew to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added weeks after the crash.
- Imaging and exam findings clearly confirm the injury.
- Records show long-standing treatment for the same condition before the crash; most of the current complaints come from it.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
text: Treatment summary, prepared by the treating provider. The patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection, with a wrist fracture that is consistent in type and mechanism with the force of that crash. Imaging and examination findings clearly confirm the fracture. Over the course of care the patient attended forty visits, a volume well above what is typical for this injury, with visits occurring almost daily for a period. Additional body regions were reported and added to the treatment plan several weeks after the collision. Review of the outside records shows the patient was under treatment for the same condition before the collision, and much of the current complaint appears to stem from that earlier, ongoing problem rather than from the fracture alone. The billing records show no repeated or duplicate charges for the same services. Recommendations are to continue orthopedic follow-up for the fracture, reassess the remaining complaints once the prior condition is clarified, and coordinate with the patient's prior providers.
